# Quick Start

If you're new to Six.SvgKit, start with these basic examples:

## Load and Optimize an SVG

```csharp
using Six.SvgKit;
using Six.SvgKit.Optimizer;

// Load SVG and apply basic optimizations
var result = Svg.FromFile("input.svg")
    .Query()
    .DefaultOptimizations()
    .Build();

// Save optimized version
result.ToFile("optimized.svg");

// Check the results
result.SizeComparisonInPercentage(percentage =>
    Console.WriteLine($"File size reduced by {percentage:F1}%"));
```

## Create an Icon from SVG

```csharp
// Optimize for icon use
var iconResult = Svg.FromFile("logo.svg")
    .Query()
    .MonoIconsOptimizations(width: 32, height: 32)
    .Build();

// Save as SVG and convert to PNG
iconResult.ToFile("icon.svg");
iconResult.ModifiedSvg.ToBitmapFile(MagickFormat.Png24, "icon.png", 32, 32);
```

## Process Multiple Files

```csharp
var svgFiles = Directory.GetFiles("input", "*.svg");

Parallel.ForEach(svgFiles, file =>
{
    var result = Svg.FromFile(file)
        .Query()
        .DefaultOptimizations()
        .Build();
    
    var outputPath = Path.Combine("output", Path.GetFileName(file));
    result.ToFile(outputPath);
});
```

# What You'll Learn

Through these examples, you'll discover how to:

- **Load and manipulate** SVG files from strings and files
- **Apply optimizations** to reduce file sizes significantly
- **Convert formats** to create bitmap versions of your SVGs
- **Process files in batches** for efficient workflows
- **Integrate Six.SvgKit** into your applications and build processes
- **Handle errors** and edge cases gracefully
- **Monitor performance** and optimization results
- **Create custom** optimization pipelines for specific needs

# Quick Start

Let's start with a simple example that demonstrates the basic workflow of Six.SvgKit:

## 1. Import Namespaces

```csharp
using Six.SvgKit;
using Six.SvgKit.Optimizer; // If using optimization features
```

## 2. Load an SVG

You can load SVG content from a file or string:

```csharp
// From file
var svg = Svg.FromFile("path/to/your/icon.svg");

// From string
var svgString = @"<svg xmlns=""http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"" width=""24"" height=""24"">
    <circle cx=""12"" cy=""12"" r=""10"" fill=""blue"" />
</svg>";
var svg = Svg.FromString(svgString);
```

## 3. Basic Operations

```csharp
// Get the SVG as a string
string svgOutput = svg.ToSvg();

// Save to file
svg.ToSvgFile("output.svg");

// Convert to byte array
byte[] svgBytes = svg.ToBytes();
```

## 4. Apply Optimizations

```csharp
// Apply basic optimizations
var optimizedSvg = svg
    .Query()
    .DefaultOptimizations() // Requires Six.SvgKit.Optimizer
    .Build();

// Get the optimized SVG
string optimizedOutput = optimizedSvg.ModifiedSvg.ToSvg();
```

# Configuration Options

Six.SvgKit provides several configuration options to customize its behavior:

## Output Compression

Control how SVG output is formatted:

```csharp
var svg = Svg.FromFile("input.svg");

// Enable compression (removes whitespace)
svg.CompressOutput = true;

// Disable XML declaration
svg.OmmitXmlDeclaration = true;

string compressedSvg = svg.ToSvg();
```

## Metadata Tracking

Add metadata to track SVG instances during batch processing:

```csharp

var svg = Svg.FromFile("input.svg")
```

# Usage Patterns

Learn how to effectively combine these classes and methods to create powerful SVG processing workflows.

## Method Chaining

Six.SvgKit is designed for method chaining to create readable optimization pipelines:

```csharp
var result = Svg.FromFile("input.svg")
    .Query()
    .ConvertShapesToPaths()
    .MergePaths()
    .RoundPathSegments(2)
    .RemoveEmptyNodes()
    .CleanupAttributes()
    .CompressOutput()
    .Build()
    .SizeComparisonInPercentage(p => Console.WriteLine($"Reduced by {p:F1}%"));

result.ToFile("output.svg");
```

## Conditional Operations

Apply operations based on conditions:

```csharp
var builder = svg.Query();

if (optimizeForWeb)
{
    builder.DefaultOptimizations();
}

if (targetFormat == "icon")
{
    builder.MonoIconsOptimizations();
}

var result = builder.Build();
```

Process multiple files efficiently:

```csharp
var files = Directory.GetFiles("input", "*.svg");

Parallel.ForEach(files, file =>
{

        .Query()
        .DefaultOptimizations()
        .Build();
```

**Six SvgKit** is a modern .NET library designed for **parsing, manipulating, and optimizing SVG (Scalable
Vector Graphics) files**.

Whether you need to optimize SVG files for web performance, batch process icon sets, or manipulate SVG content 
programmatically, **Six SvgKit** provides an intuitive API with powerful optimization capabilities.

</Aside>

<CardGrid>

    Parse SVG files from strings or files with a fluent API. Access and modify SVG elements, attributes, and structure with ease.
  </Card>
  
  <Card title="Advanced Optimization" icon="rocket">
    Built-in optimization techniques including path merging, shape conversion, attribute cleanup, and compression for smaller file sizes.
  </Card>
  
  <Card title="Batch Processing" icon="list-format">

    Convert SVG files to various bitmap formats (PNG, WebP) using ImageMagick integration for versatile output options.
  </Card>
</CardGrid>


# Common Use Cases

**Six SvgKit** is perfect for:

- **Icon Set Optimization**: Batch optimize icon collections for web applications
- **SVG Cleanup**: Remove unnecessary elements and attributes from SVG files
- **Format Conversion**: Convert SVG files to bitmap formats for different platforms
- **Build Pipeline Integration**: Automate SVG processing in CI/CD workflows
- **Web Performance**: Reduce SVG file sizes for faster page loading
- **Accessibility**: Ensure SVG files meet accessibility standards

# Library Architecture

**Six SvgKit** consists of two main packages:

## Six.SvgKit (Core Library)
The core library provides fundamental SVG parsing, manipulation, and serialization capabilities:
- SVG document parsing and AST representation
- Element and attribute manipulation
- Query builder for complex operations
- File I/O and format conversion

## Six.SvgKit.Optimizer (Optimization Extensions)
The optimizer package extends the core library with advanced optimization techniques:
- Path optimization and merging
- Shape-to-path conversion

# Overview

Six.SvgKit.Optimizer provides powerful tools for reducing SVG file sizes while maintaining visual quality. This guide covers optimization strategies, techniques, and best practices for different use cases.

# Understanding SVG Optimization

SVG optimization involves removing unnecessary elements, simplifying paths, and normalizing attributes while preserving the visual appearance and functionality of the graphic. The goal is to achieve the smallest possible file size without compromising quality.

## Why Optimize SVGs?

<CardGrid>
  <Card title="Faster Loading" icon="rocket">
    Smaller files load faster, improving user experience and Core Web Vitals scores.
  </Card>
  
  <Card title="Reduced Bandwidth" icon="down-caret">
    Lower file sizes mean less data transfer, especially important for mobile users.
  </Card>
  
  <Card title="Better Performance" icon="star">
    Optimized SVGs render faster and use less memory in browsers and applications.
  </Card>
  
  <Card title="Storage Savings" icon="open-book">
    Smaller files require less storage space, reducing hosting costs and backup sizes.
  </Card>
</CardGrid>

# Optimization Presets

Six.SvgKit provides ready-made optimization presets for common scenarios.

## Default Optimizations

The `DefaultOptimizations()` method applies a comprehensive set of safe optimizations suitable for most SVGs:

```csharp
using Six.SvgKit;
using Six.SvgKit.Optimizer;

var result = Svg.FromFile("input.svg")
    .Query()
    .DefaultOptimizations()
    .Build();

// Save optimized SVG
result.ToFile("optimized.svg");

// Check the size reduction
result.SizeComparisonInPercentage(percentage =>
    Console.WriteLine($"Size reduced by {percentage:F1}%"));
```

**What DefaultOptimizations includes:**
- Remove XML declaration
- Remove empty nodes and attributes
- Remove empty text and containers
- Collapse unnecessary groups
- Clean up attribute values
- Compress output

## Monochromatic Icons Optimization

For icon sets and simple graphics, use `MonoIconsOptimizations()`:

```csharp
var result = Svg.FromFile("icon.svg")
    .Query()
    .MonoIconsOptimizations(width: 24, height: 24, decimalPlaces: 2)
    .Build();
```

**Parameters:**
- `width`: Target width (default: 24)
- `height`: Target height (default: 24)  
- `decimalPlaces`: Coordinate precision (default: 2)

**Additional optimizations for icons:**
- Convert shapes to paths
- Merge similar paths
- Round path coordinates
- Remove viewBox attribute
- Set standard fill attributes

```csharp
var result = svg.Query()
```

# Introduction

Cleanup operations remove unnecessary elements, attributes, and content that don't contribute to the visual output, resulting in cleaner and smaller SVG files.

# Remove Empty Elements

## Remove Empty Nodes

Clean up elements that don't contribute to the visual output:

```csharp
svg.Query()
    .RemoveEmptyNodes()
    .Build();
```

**Examples of removed elements:**
- `<g></g>` - Empty groups
- `<defs></defs>` - Empty definitions
- `<metadata></metadata>` - Empty metadata
- Self-closing elements with no useful attributes

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="Before">
    ```xml
    <svg>
      <defs></defs>
      <g>
        <path d="M10,10 L20,20"/>
      </g>
      <g></g>
      <metadata></metadata>
    </svg>
    ```
  </TabItem>
  
  <TabItem label="After">
    ```xml
    <svg>
      <g>
        <path d="M10,10 L20,20"/>
      </g>
    </svg>
    ```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

# Structure Optimization

## Collapse Groups

Remove unnecessary group elements that don't add semantic value:

```csharp

    .CollapseGroups()
```

# Complete Cleanup Pipeline

Here's a comprehensive cleanup workflow:

```csharp
public static SvgResult CleanupSvg(Svg svg)
{
    return svg.Query()
        .RemoveEmptyNodes()          // Remove empty elements
        .RemoveEmptyAttributes()     // Remove empty attributes
        .RemoveEmptyText()           // Remove whitespace-only text
        .RemoveEmptyContainers()     // Remove empty containers
        .CollapseGroups()            // Remove unnecessary groups
        .CleanupAttributes()         // Normalize attribute values
        .Build();
}

// Usage
var result = CleanupSvg(svg);
result.SizeComparisonInPercentage(p => 
    Console.WriteLine($"Cleanup saved {p:F1}%"));
```

# Advanced Cleanup Techniques

## Selective Cleanup

```csharp
// Clean up everything except specific attributes
var result = svg.Query()
    .SelectAttributes(
        key => key != "id" && key != "class", // Keep ID and class
        (node, key, value) => {
            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value)) {
                node.RemoveAttribute(key);
            }
        }
    )
    .RemoveEmptyNodes()
    .CollapseGroups()
    .Build();
```

## Conditional Cleanup

```csharp
public static SvgResult SmartCleanup(Svg svg)
{
    var builder = svg.Query();
    
    // Always do basic cleanup
    builder.RemoveEmptyAttributes()
           .RemoveEmptyText();
    
    // Check if we have many groups
    var groupCount = svg.Query()
        .Select(n => n.Name == "g")
        .ToList()
        .Count;
    
    if (groupCount > 3)
    {
        // Many groups - be aggressive about collapsing
        builder.CollapseGroups();
    }
    
    // Always clean up at the end
    builder.RemoveEmptyNodes()
           .CleanupAttributes();
    
    return builder.Build();
}
```

## Preserve Important Elements

```csharp
// Cleanup while preserving accessibility and semantic elements
var result = svg.Query()
    .Select(node => {
        // Don't remove nodes with accessibility attributes
        if (node.Attributes.ContainsKey("aria-label") ||
            node.Attributes.ContainsKey("role") ||
            node.Attributes.ContainsKey("title"))
        {
            return false; // Don't select for removal
        }
        return true; // Can be cleaned up
    })
    .RemoveEmptyNodes()
    .RemoveEmptyAttributes()
    .CollapseGroups()
    .CleanupAttributes()
    .Build();
```

## Cleanup Analysis

```csharp
public static void AnalyzeCleanupOpportunities(Svg svg)
{
    var nodes = svg.Query().Select(_ => true).ToList();
    
    var emptyGroups = nodes.Count(n => n.Name == "g" && !n.Children.Any());
    var emptyAttributes = nodes.Sum(n => n.Attributes.Count(attr => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(attr.Value)));
    var nestedGroups = nodes.Count(n => n.Name == "g" && n.Parent?.Name == "g");
    
    Console.WriteLine($"Cleanup opportunities:");
    Console.WriteLine($"- Empty groups: {emptyGroups}");
    Console.WriteLine($"- Empty attributes: {emptyAttributes}");
    Console.WriteLine($"- Nested groups: {nestedGroups}");
    
    if (emptyGroups + emptyAttributes + nestedGroups > 0)
    {
        Console.WriteLine("Consider running cleanup operations");
    }
}
```
